jobDescription: The payments authorisation service approves or declines the bank's card transactions in real time. The Lead Engineer is the technical lead of the authorisation team: owns the service's technical roadmap, signs the design reviews for changes to the authorisation path, leads the incident reviews for authorisation outages, and mentors the team's engineers. The bank requires prior experience as technical lead of a real-time payments or comparable transaction service, with at least six years of software engineering, and the bank's secure development certification for the payments domain. Reports to the head of payments engineering; works with the fraud team, the card scheme liaison and the platform SRE group.
requirements: Has been the technical lead of a real-time payments or comparable transaction service, signing its design reviews.
At least six years of software engineering.
Holds the bank's secure development certification for the payments domain.
Leads incident reviews for service outages under a documented incident review process.
Mentors the team's engineers and documents the boundaries of each design review.

evidence.text: Lead Engineer and technical lead of the card authorisation service at a retail bank since 2022, signing the design reviews for changes to the authorisation path; software engineer and senior software engineer on the same service from 2017 to 2022; eight years of software engineering in all.
Secure development certification for the payments domain held since 2021 under the bank's secure development programme, renewed 2024; certificate available in the bank's learning record.
Led the incident reviews for the four authorisation outages of the last three years under the payments incident review process, with the review reports in the incident register.
Owner of the service's technical roadmap since 2022, reviewed with the head of payments engineering each quarter.
Mentored the team's six engineers under the engineering mentoring scheme and wrote the boundary note of each signed design review, stating what the review did not cover.

Work sample: two signed design reviews with their boundary notes, one incident review report and the certification record extract, with the incident register and design repository references as a verification trail.

Recruiter screen: candidate said he has been the technical lead signing the authorisation design reviews since 2022, holds the payments secure development certification, and has been on the service since 2017; the split he gave matches the resume.
Hiring manager pre-read: the head of payments engineering asks the packet to cite the signed design reviews, the incident review reports and the certification record.

propositions.text: The candidate has been Lead Engineer and technical lead of a retail bank's card authorisation service since 2022, signing the design reviews for changes to the authorisation path, after software engineer and senior software engineer roles on the same service from 2017 to 2022, eight years of software engineering in all.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the signed design reviews document the lead role and the years.

propositions.text: The candidate holds the bank's secure development certification for the payments domain since 2021, renewed in 2024, led the incident reviews for four authorisation outages under the payments incident review process, and owns the service's technical roadmap.
propositions.rationale: The resume, the certification record and the incident review report document the certification, the reviews and the roadmap.

propositions.text: The candidate mentored the team's six engineers under the engineering mentoring scheme and wrote the boundary note of each signed design review.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the work sample document the mentoring and the boundary notes.

gold.expectedGap: None; the materials document the lead role, the years, the certification, the incident reviews and the mentoring.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: The lead role, the years and the certification are documented in the resume, the signed reviews and the certification record; the earlier engineer years are shown separately.
